Botswana elephant mystery

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
While Botswana has been in lockdown for COVID-19 hundreds of elephants have mysteriously died in the Okavango Delta, we investigate why

Summary:
An unprecedented amount of Elephants have mysteriously died in the Okavango delta, Botswana since May 2020.

On the 25th of May Elephants without borders flew over the Okavango and discovered 165 Elephant Carcasses. In June a second flight revealed new carcasses bringing the total, according to them, to 365 mysteriously dead elephants.
Mike Chase the director of the project says that some of the animals appeared to have died abruptly and landed face forward. They observed some animals walking in circles, appearing to be disorientated and others dragging their hind legs, which potentially means they were paralysed by whatever was killing the elephants.
Poaching has been ruled out, as all the elephants tusks were in place. Some conservationists say it's due to starvation, because of an overpopulation of Elephants in Botswana.
Niall from National Park Rescue strongly disagree with this hypothesis, he is gravely concerned as Bots is home to 1/3 of the worlds remaining elephant population and last week more carcasses were found.

Script:








Vo: Botswana is home to 1/3 of all the elephants left in Africa, it is by the far the biggest and most important elephant herd left on earth.
So when hundreds of elephants mysteriously start dying in the Okavango Delta it quickly becomes an investigation of global importance

Upsound news

link: For years the Botswanan government has taken extreme measures to keep elephants safe, dedicating nearly 40% of the countries landmass to conservation. Botswana has always been a safe space for elephants, as poaching increases in neighbouring countries.


Vo: But alarm bells were raised about the safety of Botswana’s Elephants when in May a local NGO was flying over a area north of the Okavango Delta when they discovered 169 elephant carcasses and as the months have gone by the numbers have continued to increase

NIALL:
by the end of May when the first survey was undertaken. One hundred and sixty nine carcasses identified.
This is now a mass die off approaching the scale that we haven't seen before. the 20th of June that number had increased to three hundred and fifty six.
So it is over doubled from what it was three and a half four weeks before.. This is no longer just a parochial small issue in northern Botswana. This is now something that the world really cares about.

VO: Dr Niall McCann is a natgeo explorer, biologist and the Director of Conservation for National Park Rescue, He has been working with local NGO’s since they first spotted the elephant carcasses


NIALL: when you're looking at some of the carcasses some of them just dropped straight onto that front directly forwards as if they've been shot in the head and died instantly. And that's me indicating that some of these animals may very very quickly they're collapsing almost mid step

LINK: After years of research scientists believe that the emotional attachment that elephants form with family members may rival our own. They grieve loss and they cry salt tears. In fact years after a heard members passes they have been seen to return to the site where they died and hold a silent pause


NIALL: if any animal that is that sociable intelligent loses that many of its number it's going to have a massive psychological effect. Elephants have a brain four times the size of ours.
So for them to have witnessed 400 or more of their family dying over the last little while they must be absolutely terrified. I can't imagine what's

VO: As soon as this story broke specialist around the world starting asking questions and demanding answers from Botswana’s wildlife department. A team of local experts were sent out in the beginning of May to start investigating. Dr Cyril Taolo is the acting deputy director

TAOLO:
How they went into the field to get samples. Needed helicopters as the animals were in remote areas

Clair question back about poaching
Taolo:
It's clear that because the elephants were found with their ivory we could not
Put this down to poaching
Purposes
There was ALSO no evidence to suggest that there was poisoning because we did not find evidence of other scavengers of any kind. Normally when it's poisoning you expect to find other animals also being killed by that same event.

VO: However Dr. Mccann isn’t convinced that poisoning for either poaching or BY Local farmers trying to protect their crops can be completely ruled out at this point

NIALL:
there are other poisons aluminium sulfide and others that don't have a secondary effect. So for me poison is as likely as a pathogen.

VO: Other conservationists have speculated that this could have been starvation due to an over population of elephants in Botswana, but both Dr McCann and Dr Taolo agree on the fact that this is not a plausible theory

NIALL: when one looks at the caucuses and sees it the condition of the caucuses does not indicate an animal that's died from starvation and also starvation would affect young animals first and not the adults.
Overpopulation really is a product of our lack of imagination
Back in the fifteen hundreds. There were 26 million elephants in Africa. The idea that Botswana is overpopulated because it's got 130000 elephants I think is simply a product of our shifting baseline.





VO: what evidence has been published actually indicates that the population is below what you might call an ecological threshold
Experts turned their investigation to potential environmental factors in the area where the majority of the carcasses were found

TAOLO:
What was interesting was that these elephants were dying predominantly within 100 meters of water is the water source
So we were keen to see if there was a link between the elephants and these water are these water sources. And that is why we've we collected samples from the water

VO: Through their initial samples the government of Botswana were able to immediately rule out naturally occurring Anthrax, which killed nearly 100 elephants in 2019. Further samples collected from the environment and fresh carcasses have been sent to 5 countries around the world for investigation, but not all results are in.
While investigations continue on the ground in Botswana, conservationists and scientists debate other potential causes of death

NIALL: there are three(DELETE?) strong competing theories at the moment
The first is that this is a pathogen so a disease which is affecting the elephants and nothing else.
And what this is doing is it's killing elephants of all ages
It could be something else. But but who knows.

TOALA’S ASNWER ABOUT TEST RESULTS NOT VIRAL, BUT AWAITING MORE TEST RESULTS
From the results so far we think it is a natural toxin

VO: McCann and other experts are not convinced that a natural toxin is a viable cause of death

NIALL:. The least likely is that this is a natural toxin something like Blue-green algae but it would kill everything blue green algae
So a natural poison I would expect other animals to also be dying. Two dead hippos dead rhinos dead antelope.

VO: Its been 3 months since the first carcasses where discovered, but the Botswana wildlife department is still waiting for test results, which they largely attribute to COVID-19 restrictions. For now the reason why these elephants are dying is still unknown

Niall:
more elephants are going to die. I would say and I hope I'm wrong. But I am very fearful that not only a more elephant is going to die but that this is accelerating because remember the first carcasses were spotted in March one or two here or there and then by the end of May. There were 169 by the end of April but more than more than doubled. So I'm concerned that this is going to be increasing at an exponential rate.
And there's a population of elephants in the area between 15 and 18 thousands if that elephant population is all affected. That's between 3 and 4 percent of the global population just wiped out in the blink of an eye.

According to McCann a devastating nearly 400 Elephants have lost their lives, so the search to find answers grows more urgent

Ending as per how we have it from Taolo: They have not found any fresh carcasses and they will continue to protect the elephants
